 UWM scholarship & FAFSA season is here & students are encouraged to apply 
 by 
 UWM Postie 
 November 19, 2026 November 19, 2026 
 Credit: via Creative Commons Liscenses 
 UW-Milwaukee’s scholarship awarding cycle for Academic Year 2027-28 is underway. UWM offers student scholarships based on a variety of factors, including academic merit, financial need, leadership and service. The  Panther Scholarship Portal is the place to find and apply for UWM scholarships. 
 The 2027-28 FAFSA is also open . This is the first step in determining whether you are eligible for state and federal financial aid. Go to FAFSA.gov and log in with your FSA ID and password. Check out the UWM Student Financial Services site for more information or to connect with a financial aid advisor.
 Five steps to take to be considered for scholarships: 
 Complete and submit the  Panther Scholarship Portal General Application. Even if you completed this before, you need to resubmit it each academic year.
 Your school/college may have a secondary application. Complete this to apply for scholarships in your major.
 Check out Recommended Opportunities in the  Panther Scholarship Portal . You can also find additional scholarship opportunities by filtering by major, department and other categories.
 Submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid ( FAFSA ) every year. Many scholarships are need-based, and submitting the FAFSA is a requirement or preference for consideration.
 Apply early and check back often. Scholarships for next year are typically awarded by Mar. 1, so winter months are the best time to complete your application(s).
 The most common application deadline for scholarships is Feb. 1 .
 Check your UWM email regularly for announcements about open applications and explore the  Panther Scholarship Portal for more information on start dates and new opportunities. Additional information – including a  Getting Started with Scholarships Guide – is available at  scholarships.uwm.edu .
 If you have questions, please  contact the Office of Student Scholarships .
 Gov. Evers Proclaims National Scholarship Month in Wisconsin
 The Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions (DFI) , together with the Wisconsin Higher Educational Aids Board (HEAB) , announced Gov. Tony Evers proclaimed the month of November as National Scholarship Month in Wisconsin. The proclamation is part of a nationwide effort to raise awareness about the vital role scholarships play in helping students and families make education after high school more affordable, reduce financial barriers, and minimize the amount students may need to borrow.
 “Higher education should be attainable and affordable for every Wisconsinite who chooses to pursue it, and scholarships help ensure students across our state can pursue their goals and dreams,” said Gov. Evers. “During National Scholarship Month, I encourage students and families to explore scholarship opportunities and take advantage of the resources available to help make their educational and career goals a reality.”
 Gov. Evers, DFI Secretary Baumann, and HEAB Executive Secretary DeVooght Blaney offer the following tips to help students and families find and apply for scholarships:
 Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA ® ). The FAFSA ® is an important first step in planning how to pay for education after high school. Students must complete the FAFSA ® to be considered for Wisconsin state financial aid, including programs such as the Wisconsin Grant. The FAFSA ® may also be required for institutional and other forms of financial aid. Students and families should complete the FAFSA ® as early as possible each year.
 Start searching early and keep searching. Scholarship opportunities are available throughout the year, and eligibility requirements vary. High school students should check with their school counselors and colleges or universities, while current college students should continue checking with their school’s financial aid office. Students can also explore scholarships offered by local businesses, community organizations, employers, foundations, professional organizations, and other groups.
 Apply for more than one scholarship. A scholarship does not have to cover the entire cost of education to make a difference. Smaller awards can add up and help pay for tuition, books, supplies, fees, and other education expenses.
 Look beyond grades and athletics. Scholarships may be based on academic achievement, but many also recognize community service, leadership, career interests, extracurricular activities, hobbies, talents, family or community connections, and other accomplishments. Students should look for scholarships that match their individual experiences and interests.
 Beware of scholarship scams. Legitimate scholarship opportunities generally do not require students to pay a fee simply to apply, guarantee that an applicant will receive money, or pressure students to provide personal or financial information immediately. Students should research an organization before applying and be cautious of any scholarship offers that sound too good to be true.
 For additional information on finding and applying for scholarships, college affordability, and the Wisconsin 529 College Savings Program, visit the DFI’s  college and career readiness ​ webpage.
 For information on Wisconsin’s financial aid, including scholarship, grant, and loan programs, tuition reciprocity agreements, and tuition capitation contracts, visit HEAB’s website .
